fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Plan-review criterion prompts ship with no behavioral regression oracle. Of the 50
plan-review criteria returned by `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')`,
only 12 have an eval spec across `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` and `.rebar/evals/`. A
contributor editing any of the other rubrics under `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` learns
nothing if the edit reintroduces a false positive or drops a catch. ADR 0109 delivered a way
to MEASURE a proposed change (the three-tier replay harness); it did not deliver an assertion
of any criterion's required behavior on concrete material.

The material already exists. The committed manifest
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/corpus-2026-08-30.manifest.json` records 6,482
sidecar rows (`verified_ratio` 0.9568), and
`plan_replay/corpus.py` reconstructs each row's at-review plan text. `plan_review/sidecar.py`
retains, per finding, the `criteria` list, `cohort` (`sidecar.py:667-672`), `norm_id`,
`decision`, and `decision_margin` — enough to state, for a real plan, which criteria fired,
and — via the per-finding `cohort` set — which criteria were routed yet stayed silent.

## Approach

Mine that corpus offline into per-criterion fire/no-fire eval fixtures on real plans, and
admit a fixture only after it reproduces against current code.

**No-fire evidence predicate.** The sidecar persists only findings that FIRED, so silence is
an ABSENCE inference, never on its own a valid `expect: pass` case: silence from the criterion
never being routed to that plan is indistinguishable from silence from finding nothing. The
selector admits a plan as no-fire evidence for criterion C only when C appears in the `cohort`
set of some finding recorded for that plan (`sidecar.py:667-672`, proving C was routed) AND no
finding on that plan cites C; a row with a MISSING `cohort` key is treated as unknown and
skipped, never emitted as `expect: pass` (the sidecar contract: missing cohort is unknown,
never an empty set). No-fire reproduction consensus ranges over the equal-`material_fingerprint`
reviews meeting this predicate; the selector owns it, the emitter transcribes it.

**Only inline-runnable criteria are mined.** `eval_solver.py:100-140` has three runner
paths: generic criteria run over inline plan text, `CONTAINER_CRITERIA` (G3/G4/decomp-shape)
require a `children` payload, and ISF RAISES on any inline fixture. Both non-inline classes
still carry a `cohort` tag, so the selector EXCLUDES them from inline mining and the
self-healing loop files an `unreliable-criterion:` ticket (reason: finder not inline-runnable)
for each; the admission runner treats a fixture whose finder rejects its shape as
WITHHELD-with-reason, never a hard error.

This fits because the fixture is what the existing machinery already consumes:
`rebar criteria eval` runs a criterion's cases through its real Pass-1 finder
(`eval_solver.py:139-142`) via the validated `.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml` seam
(`eval.py:69-78`). A fixture adds zero production tokens, cannot
bias a live review, and composes with the ADR 0109 harness rather than duplicating it.

This epic REPLACES its earlier R-4 framing (examples injected into reviewer prompts): the
Pass-1 rubric is assembled into `instructions` AFTER the cache breakpoint
(`pass1.py:283-298`), so prompt-resident examples re-bill on every chunk forever, and a false
positive used as both prompt example and eval case makes the eval measure nothing.

## Non-goals

- Injecting anything into reviewer prompts. No file under `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`
  changes in this epic.
- Fixtures for criteria that already have a spec. `eval.py:69-78` resolves a project spec
  as a REPLACEMENT for the packaged one, so writing one there would delete the packaged
  cases.
- Shipping rebar's fixtures as packaged core for other projects. The tooling is the reusable
  artifact; a project overriding criteria owns its own evals, as it already owns its tests.
- Closing the drift the admission run discovers. Each entry becomes a follow-on ticket
  linked `discovered_from` this epic.
- Per-finding true/false-positive labelling or human adjudication (the 2026-07-16 attempt
  was invalidated at ~79% contaminated labels,
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/README.md:112-118`; not retried here).
- Restructuring the prompt cache so eval prefixes become cacheable.

## Budget

Epic ceiling **$450** including a $75 reserve, enforced by the parameterized ledger and
allocated per child: ledger $0, selector $0, emitter $0, admission runner $250,
change-triggered execution $25, self-healing loop $100, ADR/docs $0. The admission bootstrap
central estimate is $112 (band $68-$229) at the per-call rates in
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/ledger.jsonl`. Steady-state cost after this epic
is zero unless a rubric changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A no-fire (`expect: pass`) case for criterion C is emitted only when C is in the
      `cohort` set of some finding on that plan AND no finding on that plan cites C; a row
      with a missing `cohort` key is skipped, never emitted; verified by `pytest` over a
      synthetic corpus with an in-cohort silent plan (emitted), a never-in-cohort plan
      (skipped), a missing-cohort row (skipped), and a container/ISF-class criterion
      (excluded from inline mining).
- [x] Every plan-review criterion that `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')`
      reports and that had no eval spec when this epic opened either has a spec file under
      `.rebar/evals/`, or an open ticket titled `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>`
      recording why it has none; verified by a script that sets the routing key set against
      `ls .rebar/evals/ src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` and the open-ticket titles, and exits
      non-zero if any criterion is in neither set.
- [x] No fixture enters `.rebar/evals/` without having reproduced against current code, and
      the candidates that failed to reproduce are recorded with both their historical and
      observed behavior; verified by the committed drift report plus the admission run's
      admitted/withheld counts.
- [x] A criterion's fixtures execute when that criterion's rubric file changes, and the
      criteria covered by this epic do not join the existing weekly live sweep; verified by
      `grep` of the resolved weekly spec list showing none of the new prompt ids.
- [x] A run whose pre-flight estimate would exceed the epic ceiling is refused before it
      issues any model call; verified by `pytest` over the ledger refusal test.
- [x] No file under `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` is modified by this epic; verified by
      `git diff --stat origin/main..HEAD -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` producing no output.
- [x] The mining and admission protocol is recorded as an ADR under `docs/adr/` and
      referenced from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`; verified by `grep -q` for the ADR filename
      in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Child decomposition

Each acceptance criterion above is owned by at least one child, non-overlapping:

- No-fire predicate AC -> the selector (owns/applies the cohort + no-finding predicate) and
  the emitter (transcribes no-fire candidates to `expect: pass`).
- Coverage AC -> the selector (trustworthy candidates), the emitter (validated specs) and
  the admission runner (writes survivors); residual gaps + container/ISF criteria -> the
  self-healing loop, which files the `unreliable-criterion:` tickets.
- Reproduction/drift AC -> the admission runner.
- Change-triggered execution AC -> the change-triggered execution child.
- Budget-refusal AC -> the ledger parameterization child, consumed by the admission runner.
- Untouched-prompts AC -> a constraint on every child; no child edits a rubric.
- ADR AC -> the ADR and docs child.

Ordering: selector -> emitter; emitter + ledger -> admission runner; admission runner ->
change-triggered execution + self-healing loop; ADR/docs lands last.
